claim: Palantir Technologies was seeded by In-Q-Tel, the CIA's venture-capital arm, which made two rounds of investment totaling more than $2 million in the young company — the only outside money it took for years. From 2005 to 2008 the CIA was Palantir's sole customer, alpha-testing and refining its data-analysis software before the company expanded to other agencies and commercial clients. Palantir was co-founded in 2003–2004 by PayPal veterans Peter Thiel and Alex Karp; its early product work drew on the same intelligence data-fusion problem that Total Information Awareness had been built to solve.

sources.label: Forbes (Andy Greenberg) — "How A 'Deviant' Philosopher Built Palantir, A CIA-Funded Data-Mining Juggernaut" (August 14, 2013). In-Q-Tel's two funding rounds and the 2005–2008 sole-customer period.
sources.quote: From 2005 to 2008 the CIA was Palantir's patron and only customer, alpha-testing and evaluating its software.

sources.label: Forbes (Andy Greenberg), same article — the In-Q-Tel referral and the size of the CIA venture investment.
